correctness.rationale: Two complete standalone programs reconstruct the identical 11-vertex, 20-edge object via different definitions. Complete closed-neighborhood face enumeration finds 1435 faces with facet dimensions five to seven. Fixed vertex toggling yields 715 ordinary pairs and precisely four critical cells in dimensions 0,5,6,6; the 6881 Hasse arrows form a DAG on all 1434 nonempty faces. Exact signed integral Morse recurrence gives boundary [0,0]. Since the five-skeleton is a single 5-sphere and pi_5(S5)=Z, both 6-cell attaching maps are nullhomotopic. Distinct brute-force facet and prime-2/prime-3 simplicial rank check gives unreduced Betti (1,0,0,0,0,1,2,0); prime arithmetic only corroborates the integral proof.

value.rationale: The 11-vertex Grötzsch graph is a canonical, uniquely smallest triangle-free four-chromatic graph and the first four-chromatic member of Mycielski’s sequence, hence a mathematically natural nonchordal test case. Its complete dominance complex is nonpure, has distinct adjacent degrees of integral homology, and is provably an integral wedge of 5- and 6-spheres, neither an automatic instance of the chordal theorem nor merely a recomputation of a known table. The exact attaching-map information is useful for comparison with further Mycielski constructions, although no infinite-family result is claimed.
